summary: Describes how the Independent Submissions Editor currently handles requests for IANA actions on documents in the Independent Submission stream. It complements RFC 4846.

eli5.summary: Some documents come outside the usual IETF path and still need entries in official lists. This explains how those requests are handled.

subtitle: Rules for IANA registries in documents outside the main IETF track.

tldr.problem: The Independent Submission Stream publishes RFCs outside the normal IETF process. When these documents request IANA actions (new code points or registries), the rules must be clear.
tldr.mechanism: Independent Stream documents can request code points from existing registries if the allocation policy permits, but creation of new registries is generally forbidden except when tied to a code point request. Designated Expert review is not available for Independent Stream registries.
tldr.outcome: This RFC clarifies that Independent Stream RFCs operate under constraints designed to prevent future IETF burdens while still allowing useful registry work.

today: RFC 8726 remains in effect and is the authoritative guide for how Independent Stream documents request IANA actions. It is informational and establishes no new registries itself.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The IETF publishes RFCs through several different streams. The main stream follows the IETF Standards Process, with extensive review and consensus. The Independent Submission Stream, managed by the Independent Submissions Editor (ISE), publishes valuable but independently authored documents that do not go through IETF review.

When documents in either stream request IANA actions—assignments from existing registries or creation of new registries—the rules are different. This RFC, complementing RFC 4846 which describes Independent Stream publication, spells out exactly what IANA requests Independent Stream documents can and cannot make.
sections.eli5: Some documents are published as RFCs but not through the normal IETF approval process. This explains what kinds of IANA registry requests those independent documents are allowed to make.

sections.title: Allocations from Existing Registries
sections.content:
Independent Stream documents can request code points from existing IANA registries, but only if the registry's allocation policy permits it. The registry policies are defined in RFC 8126. Policies like "First Come First Served" and "Expert Review" are open to Independent Stream documents. However, policies requiring "IETF Review" or "Standards Action" are off-limits to Independent Stream documents because those policies by definition require IETF participation.

All requests must still follow the allocation policy of the registry—if the policy requires expert review, the designated expert must approve the request. This ensures consistency and quality across all streams.
sections.eli5: Independent Stream documents can ask for numbers from existing lists, as long as the list's rules allow it. But some lists are only for IETF documents, and Independent Stream documents cannot use those.

sections.title: Creating New IANA Registries
sections.content:
Creating a new IANA registry is generally forbidden for Independent Stream documents. The only exception is when a document requests a code point from an existing registry with an open allocation policy (Specification Required, Expert Review, RFC Required, or First Come First Served), and that code point requires a sub-registry to interpret a sub-code. For example, a new URI scheme registered in the "URI Schemes" registry might need a companion registry for parameters specific to that scheme.

Even in this narrow case, the new registry must follow strict rules. Its allocation policy can only be First Come First Served, RFC Required, Experimental, or Private Use—no policy that would require future IETF action. The document must explain the expected rate of new registrations if the policy is First Come First Served. It must also contain an escalation process for issues, and the IESG is invited to comment on advisability during conflict review.
sections.eli5: Independent Stream documents usually cannot create new official registries. The rare exception is when they register a code point and that code point needs its own small sub-registry, and only with specific rules attached.

sections.title: Designated Experts and Support
sections.content:
Some IANA registries require Designated Expert review, where an expert vetted by the IETF checks each new assignment. The ISE will not appoint Designated Experts for Independent Stream registries. This means that no new sub-registry created by an Independent Stream document can use the "Specification Required" or "Expert Review" policies—because those require expert appointments that the ISE will not maintain.

This rule exists to prevent the IETF from inheriting the burden of maintaining expert review infrastructure for registries started outside the IETF process.
sections.eli5: If a registry needs an expert to check new entries, only IETF documents can create it, because the IETF will maintain the expert. Independent Stream documents cannot create registries that need expert review.

sections.title: Status and Context
sections.content: RFC 8726 was published in November 2020 by Adrian Farrel as Independent Submissions Editor. It codifies and clarifies practices the ISE had already been following. The RFC makes plain to authors and the community the constraints on Independent Stream registry work, preventing surprises or conflicts downstream.
sections.eli5: This document puts into writing the rules the Independent Submissions Editor already follows when approving IANA registry requests.
